page: Amazon Web Services r8gn.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the ARMv9 AWS Graviton architecture with Neoverse-V2 cores. The configuration provides 4 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz with a 1:1 thread-to-core mapping, accompanied by 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of shared L3 cache. It includes 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio (8.0 GB per core). The instance includes no local storage or GPUs, relying on networked EBS storage, and features a baseline network throughput of 12 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate notable memory subsystem performance, highlighted by a PassMark memory score of 3048.49, placing it in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems. Memory throughput reaches 110.92 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 44.29 GB/sec for writes, alongside cached read speeds of 462.16 GB/sec. General compute metrics, including Geekbench single-core (1820.0) and multi-core (5893.0) along with stress-ng tests, consistently score within average mid-tier percentiles. In-memory datastores reflect balanced responsiveness, sustaining 8.54 million Redis SET operations per second and 10.12 GB/sec of static web serving throughput.

Performance tradeoffs stem from the absence of x86 vector extensions (AVX/AVX-512) and lack of hardware accelerators. CPU-based cryptographic workloads score poorly (PassMark encryption at 750.17), and LLM text generation throughput drops sharply from 89.37 tokens/sec on lightweight 135M models to 6.37 tokens/sec on 7B models. Compute density is constrained by the 4-core limit. Given its 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio and high memory bandwidth, the instance offers strong resource efficiency for medium-scale Redis or Memcached clusters, in-memory databases, and distributed ETL pipelines requiring substantial memory per thread without requiring high local NVMe throughput.
description: Amazon Web Services r8gn.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by a 4-core ARMv9 AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor clocked at 2.8 GHz, paired with 32.0 GB of RAM. Designed on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance provides dedicated single-threaded cores with an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, 12 Gbps baseline networking, and relies on network-attached storage with no local disks or hardware accelerators. Synthetic benchmarks reflect top-tier memory subsystem results, achieving 110.92 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth, 8.54 million Redis SET operations per second, and a PassMark memory score in the top decile. In contrast, cryptographic and extended vector calculations show weaker performance due to ARM architecture constraints. The hardware profile is efficient and suited for in-memory caching, mid-sized database instances, and memory-bound ETL workflows.
